source.title: SteerAct: Unlocking Action Models through Few-Shot Temporal Steering
source.authors: Kai-Chen Zhou; Zhi-Yang Li; Chong-Kai Gao; Yu-Han Wang; Wen-Long Huang; M. Wang; Fang-Neng Zhan; Man-Ling Li; Qian-Qian Wang; Mac Schwager; Zhuang Liu; Fei-Fei Li; Meng-Yu Wang; P. Liang

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE features as an interface for steering robot action models toward task success. It does not test superposition, polysemanticity, feature overlap, or the geometry of model representations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports task-success outcomes from SAE-feature steering, which are relevant to feature-based intervention in robot models but do not measure any listed version as stated. Results cited about other steering methods are not recorded as findings of this study.
record.test_reason: The study uses a pretrained TopK SAE on robot action models (π0.5, Fast-WAM) as a source of steering directions and reports only its own method's task-success rates against baselines and ablations. It does not measure feature overlap, polysemanticity, neuron-level distribution of features, or whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical. These are not LLMs, and no geometry or dimensionality of features is examined.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that a single internal SAE feature can be a useful adaptation interface for frozen action models when its intervention is guided by the unfolding execution. They also note that remaining regressions and backbone-dependent gaps limit what steering alone can achieve. They make no claims about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce or test the method of Toy Models of Superposition; it applies SAE-based temporal feature steering to frozen robot action models for task success.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary with intervention site (encoder versus action expert), temporal descriptor, number of selected features, reference-rollout budget, coefficient choice, and the use of support and failure gates.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering along one or a few selected SAE decoder directions, with reference-guided gating, raised robot task success over the frozen policy. Examples: 69.0→77.7% (RoboTwin 2.0, π0.5) and 31.1→52.2% on the real robot. Gains depended on intervention site, descriptor, gating and backbone. With no gates, success fell to 22.38% versus 23.63% frozen.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature directions in robot action models can serve as effective steering handles for task success, contingent on intervention site and timing.

record.code_released: not stated (the text says code and demo are available at “Link,” without giving a URL)
record.problems: The study is about robot action models rather than LLM representation geometry. Per-task results at n=200 are described as indicative; several aggregate ablations have no uncertainty estimates. The authors note that timing evidence comes from gate and fixed-delay ablations, not a controlled isolation of behavioral phase, and that the SAE bounds available steering directions.
record.rows_left_out: The task-by-task entries in Tables 1, 5, and 6 were not separately extracted; aggregate results and explicitly described exceptions or condition changes were retained. The paper also reports comparisons to other steering methods, but those results do not directly test the listed representation claims.

untested.parts: No toy networks; no test of feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transition or geometry.
No measurement of neuron polysemanticity or capacity competition.
No measurement of polysemantic neurons or their causes.
Not LLMs; does not measure feature spread across neurons or SAE recovery of features (no reconstruction or interpretability metrics reported).

Uses one pretrained SAE (K=8d, TopK 100) without testing completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, or canonicity. The authors note that SAE quality bounds the available steering directions, but they do not test this.
Steers along single decoder directions, which assumes 1-D features. It does not compare against multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Robotics steering-method paper that cites the SAE literature only as a tool; it is T4 for all versions. All rows correctly carry versions none. Most rows compare variants of the study's own method, and baselines such as DrVLA, COAST and DSRL-SAC are excluded as noted. Table 1's per-task entries for Fast-WAM are garbled in the extracted text, but the means in the rows match Section 4.2.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry in toy networks.
Does not measure neuron polysemanticity, capacity competition, or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not measure polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Tests robot action models, not LLMs; does not measure feature distribution across neurons or recovery of LLM features.
Uses a pretrained SAE but does not test whether its features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional subspaces; steering with decoder directions does not establish that geometry.
